devotionals.title: Be Strong and Courageous
devotionals.verse: Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.
devotionals.content: Courage is not the absence of fear; it is moving forward because God is with you. Joshua was stepping into a new season with giant responsibilities, and God's encouragement was simple: I am with you wherever you go. Take the next step today, knowing you do not walk alone.

devotionals.title: The Lord Is My Shepherd
devotionals.verse: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
devotionals.content: A shepherd knows his sheep, leads them to water and stays close in dark valleys. David could say "I shall not want" because he knew who was caring for him. When your needs feel bigger than your supply, remember that you belong to a Shepherd who provides.

devotionals.title: Come and Rest
devotionals.verse: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
devotionals.content: Jesus does not say, "Fix yourself, then come." He says, "Come." The tired, the stretched and the burdened are invited first. Rest is not a reward for finishing everything; it is a gift received from Christ. Lay down what you are carrying today and accept His rest.

devotionals.title: All Things Work Together
devotionals.verse: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
devotionals.content: This verse does not say that everything is good. It says that God is at work in everything for the good of those who love Him. The setbacks, the waiting and the surprises are not wasted. Hold on to the truth that your story is in the hands of a God who redeems.

devotionals.title: Do Not Fear
devotionals.verse: Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee.
devotionals.content: Fear grows when we feel alone. God answers fear with presence: I am with you. He does not promise that nothing hard will happen; He promises to strengthen, help and uphold us through it. Today, name what you are afraid of and place it in the hands of the One who is with you.

devotionals.title: Trusting When You Cannot See
devotionals.verse: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.
devotionals.content: We like plans we can fully see before we start. God often asks for trust one step at a time. Leaning on our own understanding means treating our limited view as the whole picture. Trust says: I do not see the road ahead, but I know the One who does, and He will direct my paths.

devotionals.title: Walking by Faith
devotionals.verse: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.
devotionals.content: Faith is not wishful thinking. It is a confident trust in a God who has proven Himself faithful throughout history and throughout your own life. Every step of obedience, even when the outcome is unclear, is an act of faith that pleases God and honours His name.

devotionals.title: Living on Mission
devotionals.verse: Go and make disciples of all nations.
devotionals.content: The Great Commission is not just for missionaries and pastors. It is the calling of every believer. You are a missionary in your school, workplace, family and community. God sends us not just to places on a map, but to the people in our everyday lives who need to hear about His love.

devotionals.title: You Are Made New
devotionals.verse: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation.
devotionals.content: The gospel is not a self-improvement plan; it is a new birth. When we come to Christ, the old is gone. We do not carry our old identity into the new life. God declares us new creations. Not improved versions of ourselves, but entirely new people, reborn in His image.

devotionals.title: Finding Peace in the Storm
devotionals.verse: Be still, and know that I am God.
devotionals.content: In a world that rewards busyness and productivity, God invites us into stillness. Not passivity, but a confident rest in the knowledge that He holds everything in His hands. When life feels overwhelming, we are not called to figure it all out. We are called to be still and trust.

devotionals.title: The Call to Repentance
devotionals.verse: Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.
devotionals.content: Repentance is not simply feeling sorry for sin; it is a decisive turn. A 180-degree change in direction. Jesus begins His ministry not with a self-help programme but with a call to repent. This is the foundation of the Christian life: acknowledging that our way is broken and choosing God's way instead.

devotionals.title: Strength in Surrender
devotionals.verse: I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.
devotionals.content: True strength is not found in our own abilities, but in yielding ourselves entirely to God. When we acknowledge our weakness, His power is made perfect in us. Paul wrote this verse from a prison cell, not a stage. Whatever you are facing today, Christ's strength is available to you.
